## Introduction

We will render a short report that reads the summary from the
`HealthWellbeing` pipeline. By the end of these 12 minutes, you should
be able to explain where a result in the report came from and identify
what a reader needs to recreate it.

You need Quarto with *knitr* and *rmarkdown*, and the completed
`meta-summary.csv` from the pipeline. If you joined here, the
instructor can provide the prepared CSV to render locally.
[Pipeline checkpoint](06_targets.qmd#targets-checkpoint)

## Inspect the report source

Open `pipelines/health_wellbeing_report.qmd` in your editor. Its YAML
header selects HTML, names the summary file, and controls how code
and output are displayed. The report's R chunk reads one row from
`meta-summary.csv`. Inline R expressions display the results and
method names recorded in that row.

The pipeline owns the analysis. The report explains its methods and
interprets the saved results. Keeping the report downstream of the
summary makes it possible to review the same result in R and HTML.

## Render the HTML report

In the Terminal at the project root, copy the source beside its
input and render the copy. Quarto runs the report as a standalone
document. The HTML output embeds its resources and can be opened
directly in a browser. The explicit execution directory lets the
standalone report read its adjacent CSV, while workshop chapters run
from the project root.

```bash
report_dir="outputs/health-wellbeing"
if [ ! -f "$report_dir/health_wellbeing_report.qmd" ]; then
  cp pipelines/health_wellbeing_report.qmd "$report_dir/"
fi
quarto render "$report_dir/health_wellbeing_report.qmd" --to html \
  --execute-dir "$report_dir"
```

Open `outputs/health-wellbeing/health_wellbeing_report.html` in your
browser. If you have an older local copy of the report source, bring
over the updated input chunk and the Methods and Provenance sections
from the template. Keep any changes you made to the surrounding text.
Run the pipeline again before rendering whenever the selected data
or analysis changes.

## Try it yourself

Find the pooled estimate, study count, and dataset version in the
report. Compare them with the matching columns in
`meta-summary.csv`. Add a plain-language sentence to the report copy
about how differences between study populations affect interpretation,
then render the copy again. Leave the estimate linked to the CSV.

## Publishing demonstration

The instructor will open an example rendered report and show how an
approved HTML file can be served from a project site or attached to a
release. Before sharing, review the report for any content that came
from data with reuse conditions. The report source, versioned analysis
code, metadata, and environment record help others understand how the
published HTML was made.

## Quarto extensions for journal articles

Quarto extensions add formats and templates for particular publishing
workflows. During the publishing demonstration, browse the
[Journal Articles extension listing](https://quarto.org/docs/extensions/listing-journals.html)
and find a format relevant to your field. Examples include:

| Extension | Article style or publisher |
| --- | --- |
| `apaquarto` | American Psychological Association, seventh edition |
| `elsevier` | Elsevier journals |
| `plos` | Public Library of Science |
| `jss` | Journal of Statistical Software |

Open an extension's repository to check its supported formats,
required software, author metadata, and usage instructions. Compare
the template with the target journal's current submission guidance.

For follow-up, create a separate article directory and start from the
[PLOS template](https://github.com/quarto-journals/plos). Run these
commands in the Terminal from the project root and follow the prompts:

```bash
mkdir health-wellbeing-article
cd health-wellbeing-article
quarto use template quarto-journals/plos
```

The template supplies an example QMD, bibliography, and extension
files. PLOS supports `plos-html` and `plos-pdf`; the PDF format also
requires a LaTeX installation. Adapt the article to read the same
pipeline summary and retain its methods and provenance fields.

Extensions are stored locally in `_extensions/`. Include that folder
with the article source in Git. For a release, record the Quarto and
extension versions alongside the R package versions in `renv.lock`.
See the Quarto guidance on installing and versioning extensions
[@quarto-managing-extensions].

## Checkpoint {#quarto-checkpoint}

The HTML shows 29 studies and their pooled estimate when the CSV is
from the full input. It names the exact pin version, Git revision,
R version, and *meta* version. You can trace the number to a field
in the pipeline output and explain how to update it after rerunning
the analysis.
